title: Response Protocol Adapter: Aligning event semantics, partial streaming, and function-call fidelity with OpenAI Responses
creator: Asha Patel
description: Design and implement an adapter layer that maps Redwood's native streaming and tool-calling model to OpenAI Responses semantics. This ticket captures behavioral differences we must reconcile (partial events, terminal event signaling, tool-call lifecycle, and structured output validation), a prioritized mitigation plan, and a runnable test harness for runtime verification.
problem_statement: Redwood's streaming model and function-calling semantics differ from the OpenAI Responses protocol in subtle but customer-visible ways: event ordering for partial tokens vs deltas, when a function call is emitted vs completed, how structured output is validated and surfaced, and how early termination/fallbacks are represented. Customers using the OpenAI Responses contract expect identical observable behavior when switching to Redwood's API or using the compatibility shim. Current gaps have produced flakey integrations and test regressions in downstream customers and internal SDKs.
scope_in_scope: Event mapping for partial and final token deltas
Function/tool-call lifecycle mapping (initiate, patch, completed) to OpenAI Responses events
Structured-output schema validation and error events
Graceful fallback semantics when a model variant cannot support a feature (e.g., missing tool binding)
End-to-end harness that replays recorded OpenAI Responses traces and asserts parity
out_of_scope: Deep changes to underlying runtime kernel scheduling
New model architecture support not already in our catalog
Billing or quota model changes for hosted API
acceptance_criteria: Adapter emits OpenAI-compatible event sequence for 95% of recorded traces in the gold corpus
Function-call tests demonstrate identical visible lifecycle events (init, patch, complete) for both Redwood native and adapted Responses mode
Structured output failures produce diagnostic events with the same fields and codes as OpenAI Responses in the test harness
No customer-facing behavior regressions on canary for 2 weeks against a sample of 10 production call routes
Performance overhead of adapter under typical load < 6% median p50 latency impact
tasks: Inventory behavioral deltas between Redwood and OpenAI Responses (complete matrix)
Design an event translation table (input events -> output events) including header metadata and error codes
Implement streaming adapter layer with pluggable transformers for partial token aggregation
Add function-call lifecycle state machine to reconcile tool bindings and callback semantics
Implement structured-output validator and mapper with human-friendly error mapping
Build a trace-driven test harness and a small corpus of canonical OpenAI Responses traces
Run canary against internal SDKs and three customer integrations
Document known lossy mappings and recommended customer mitigations in the Console
decisions: We will implement translation in the request ingress proxy rather than in model runtime to centralize compatibility logic
Partial token deltas will be aggregated into 'delta' events matching Responses semantics; adapter can emit progressive deltas if client requests streaming=true
Function-call patches will be represented as 'tool_patch' events with standardized lexicon and correlation IDs
When a model cannot produce a feature, adapter will emit a policy-backed fallback event and optionally route to a compatible variant
progress_updates: 2025-02-20: Kickoff meeting with serving, SDK, and docs — aligned on goals and acceptance criteria
2025-02-24: Completed initial delta inventory; identified 12 unique behavioral mismatches (ordering, event names, error codes)
2025-02-27: Prototype adapter implemented that maps token-stream frames to Responses-like delta events (local PR opened)
2025-03-02: Function-call state machine spec reviewed by SDK team; minor adjustments requested around correlation ids
2025-03-04: Added structured-output validator; failing cases cataloged for remediation
review_feedback: SDK: Ensure correlation IDs are stable across retries — PR comment #12
Security: Audit required for event header passthrough — see security review ticket
Platform: Prefer central config flag to enable/disable adapter per-tenant for Dedicated customers
Docs: Need example mappings for common client-side libraries (Python/JS)
prs: runtime#982: expose streaming-frame metadata to ingress
test_plan: Run the trace-driven harness across the canonical corpus (unit + integration). Smoke test with SDKs (python/js) and three internal customer integrations. Measure event order fidelity, function-call lifecycle parity, and latency overhead. Capture mismatches in a flakiness dashboard and convert top regressions to follow-up tickets.
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged rollout per-tenant. 1) internal-only canary for 72h, 2) small external canary (3 customers) for 2 weeks and monitor parity metrics, 3) broader gradual rollout. Provide an opt-out toggle and clear diagnostics in Console for observed mapping lossy cases.
risks_mitigation: Risk: Adapter introduces non-trivial latency — Mitigation: keep adapter stateless and do perf profiling early
Risk: Achieving 1:1 parity is impossible for some model/runtime combos — Mitigation: document lossy mappings and auto-fallback to compatible variants
Risk: Correlation IDs not stable across retries causing client confusion — Mitigation: design id derivation strategy and test across retry scenarios
Risk: Security leakage via passthrough headers — Mitigation: security review and whitelist headers
notes: This ticket is intentionally implementation-focused and should produce a deployable shim plus a reproducible test corpus. Follow-ups will split out any long-running runtime changes discovered during the adapter work.
